items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: And Brian Freddie. Slim had to get a lioness.

ctx.x: Ask him if this was before he was with Amos Riley or Amos Riley.

He said, was this before you was with Amos Riley? Yeah, I had to play with Amos Riley too. No, he said, was you with Batiste before Amos Riley? Oh, no way after. Amos Riley Dive used to call him Slim or stick something. Used to call him Slim for a nickname, you know. But Willie Humphrey, you know, over there, he was Willie too, and that was Slim. And Brian Freddie. Slim had to get a lioness. He didn't get a lioness, but he never had to hold him up, you know. Then he had a horn, he had two shanks. They didn't get…
Who was he with before he was with Amos Riley?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: Oh, well, some of them are like, uh, Brian Freddie, and, uh, Johnny Dot, and, uh, Jimmy Loon.

ctx.x: Tell him I want to know about the Barrel House, though. The Barrel? About the Barrel House clarinet players. He say he want to know about the Barrel House clarinet players.

Oh, well, some of them are like, uh, Brian Freddie, and, uh, Johnny Dot, and, uh, Jimmy Loon. You remember Jimmy Loon? And he's dead, too, isn't he? Yeah. And, uh, let me see, uh, and Jeff, and, uh, Big Eye Louie, and Johnny Handy. And, uh, he sure has, and, uh, Big Eye Louie, and, uh, and Johnny Handy. And, uh, then they had a whole lot of youngsters, you know, they come up with the jazz, too, you know. Yeah. I can't remember the name of it. Ask him when George Lewis began to get good. When did George Lewis…
George Lewis? Oh, he was good when he was with me and Kid Allen.
